_officialAuthorityConfirmation: The review's readiness record carries official_authority_refresh_required, and Oregon needed it more than any other Session B state: the review's own primary authority was a Justia compilation and oregon.public.law, its overall jurisdiction decision was "Additional research required before implementation", and three of its seven tracks could not be given a timing answer. The enrolled session laws were read at the Oregon Legislature's own channel on 2026-08-06 and the position changed materially. HB 2492 was enacted as Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 349, approved by the Governor on June 20, 2025, effective January 1, 2026, applying to motions filed on or after that date, and amending ORS 137.225 as previously amended by section 55, chapter 70, Oregon Laws 2024. Reading it closes four of the review's five build blockers and three of its five release blockers. The contempt tier question is answered exactly as the review predicted: ORS 137.225(1)(b)(B) places a finding of contempt for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime in the five-year tier with Class C felonies, ORS 137.225(1)(b)(D) places all other contempt findings in the one-year tier, and ORS 137.225(13)(b) supplies the definition that makes the screen workable. The dismissed-serious-charge timing question, which the review called the most important in Oregon, is answered: ORS 137.225(1)(d) makes acquittals and dismissals available at any time, subsection (9) states in terms that "There is no time limit for making an application", and no provision forcing a dismissed serious charge to wait a conviction period appears anywhere in the enacted section. Subsection (1)(d) itself is identified, closing the review's Track 7 blocker. All four conviction tiers are confirmed as the review states them. Three rules the review did not have are added: a reduced offence classification carries the reduced classification's period under ORS 137.225(1)(f); a revoked probation bars an application for three years from revocation under ORS 137.225(1)(e); and the prosecuting attorney has 120 days from filing to object under ORS 137.225(2)(a), which answers the review's open question on the objection period. The grant standard is stronger than the review describes: under ORS 137.225(3)(b) the court shall grant a motion under (1)(c) or (1)(d), and shall grant a motion under (1)(a) where no objection is received, and under ORS 137.225(3)(a) even on an objection the court shall grant unless it makes written findings by clear and convincing evidence that the person's circumstances and behaviour create a risk to public safety, considering only criminal behaviour or related regulatory violations and expressly not nonpunitive civil liability, monetary obligations or motor vehicle violations. The fee position is settled in the participant's favour: no court filing fee under ORS 137.225(1)(g), the prosecuting attorney may not charge a fee under ORS 137.225(2)(e), and where the Department of State Police performs only one record check it may charge only one fee regardless of how many counties the person files in, which the review did not have. The form build blocker is closed twice over: ORS 137.225(12) requires the State Court Administrator to create statewide motion and proposed-order forms, and Edition 1.2 retains the Oregon Judicial Department Criminal Set-Aside (Adult Cases) packet at REV-2026-01, matching the effective date, together with the OJD marijuana motion, the OJD set-aside criminal record check request and the Oregon State Police set-aside criminal history request. The review's statement that no Oregon forms were supplied and that no statewide form was confirmed is therefore superseded, and every filing track moves from the review's provisional custom_pleading to official_pdf_fill. Two findings run against the review and are recorded rather than resolved. First, the same-episode rule: the review calls it the clearest treatment of any single doctrine in the series and directs that it be preserved, but ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) as enacted disqualifies a person convicted of any other offence within the look-back period "whether or not the other conviction is for conduct associated with the same criminal episode", and the Oregon Judicial Department's own packet describes the carve-out as "traffic violations or a single violation offense" without mentioning same-episode convictions. Neither reading is adopted and no eligibility statement is made where a same-episode conviction is in play. Second, the 2025 monetary-obligations relief: the review describes Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 395 section 1 as a general rule that expired judgment remedies count as sentence completion, but the enacted text is narrower in its operative first subsection, which expires the remedies for a judgment entered in a municipal or justice court for a pre-July 1, 2015 marijuana-possession offence under one ounce, with the sentence-completion consequence in subsection (2) keyed to obligations expired "under subsection (1) of this section". That Act was approved June 24, 2025 and took effect September 26, 2025. What the refresh could not obtain: ORS 475C.397, whose text is not published in the enrolled session laws read and which only commercial compilations carry, so the marijuana track is deferred.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Set Aside the Record of an Arrest, Citation or Charge Where No Accusatory Instrument Was Filed (ORS 137.225(1)(c))
tracks.publicName: Set aside an Oregon arrest that never led to charges

controllingAuthority.summary: Where no accusatory instrument is filed, at any time after 60 days from the date the prosecuting attorney indicates that the state has elected not to proceed with a prosecution or contempt proceeding, an arrested, cited or charged person may apply to the court in the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged for an order setting aside the record of the arrest, citation or charge. The clock runs from the prosecutor's declination, not from the arrest. Under ORS 137.225(3)(b) the court shall grant a motion under this paragraph. There is no filing fee under ORS 137.225(1)(g). Oregon calls it a set-aside and there are no separate sealing and expungement tracks: the court sets aside and seals, and under ORS 137.225(4) the conviction, arrest, citation, charge or other proceeding is deemed not to have occurred and the person may answer accordingly any questions relating to its occurrence. The order reaches Oregon court and law enforcement records including the Oregon State Police LEDS system. It does not reach federal or other states' records. Under 2024 Oregon State Police policy a set-aside does not restore firearm rights; a separate restoration process is required. Two statutory carve-outs survive: under ORS 137.225(10) the deemed-not-to-have-occurred rule does not apply in a civil action where truth is an element of a claim or defence, and a party may apply for disclosure; and under ORS 137.225(11) a court may order records reopened on a prosecutor's or defendant's motion supported by affidavit showing good cause, and a prosecuting attorney may unseal a set-aside arrest, citation or charge to initiate a proceeding within the statute of limitations, on written notice to the person.

exclusions: An arrest or citation for driving while under the influence of intoxicants where the charge is dismissed as a result of the person's successful completion of a diversion agreement described in ORS 813.200. ORS 137.225(8)(a).
The dismissal of a citation for a traffic violation. ORS 137.225(8)(b).

A person who, at the time the motion is pending before the court, is under charge of commission of any crime or of contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(C).
Federal and other states' records, which ORS 137.225 cannot reach.

Under ORS 137.225(13)(a) an affidavit includes a declaration under penalty of perjury.

The proposed order, which ORS 137.225(12) requires the State Court Administrator to publish statewide alongside the motion. On entry the order contains the original arrest or citation charge, the conviction charge if different, the date of charge, the submitting agency and the disposition, and directs sealing. The judge signs it; LegalEase never completes the signature or the court's findings.

ORS 137.225(2)(c): the person forwards a full set of fingerprints to the Department of State Police on a fingerprint card or in any other manner the department specifies. This is mandatory and is the main source of delay. ORS 137.225(2)(d) sets the fee at not more than the actual cost of the record check, and provides that where the department performs only one record check it may charge only one fee regardless of how many counties the person files in.

ORS 137.225(2)(a): a copy of the motion is served on the office of the prosecuting attorney who prosecuted the matter, or who had authority to prosecute if no accusatory instrument was filed. Under ORS 137.225(2)(e) the prosecuting attorney may not charge the person a fee for performing these requirements.

The Oregon State Police set-aside criminal history request and instructions, retained in Edition 1.2, together with the OJD request for a set-aside criminal record check retained at OR-OJD-CLA-SET-ASIDE-CHECK. The LEDS criminal history fixes the offence class, the disposition and the sentence-completion dates, and is obtained before anything is drafted.

The objection diary and what follows. ORS 137.225(2)(a) gives the prosecuting attorney 120 days from the date the motion was filed to object and to notify the court and the person. Under ORS 137.225(3)(b) the court shall grant a motion under subsection (1)(c) or (1)(d), and shall grant a motion under (1)(a) if no objection is received. If an objection is received the court holds a hearing at which the victim may make a statement, and under ORS 137.225(3)(a) the court shall still grant the motion unless it makes written findings by clear and convincing evidence that the person's circumstances and behaviour create a risk to public safety.
Obtain a certified copy of the order, confirm the Oregon State Police sealed its records, and set expectations that county processing can run many months and in some places close to two years.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Set Aside the Record After an Acquittal (ORS 137.225(1)(d))
tracks.publicName: Set aside an Oregon charge you were acquitted of

controllingAuthority.summary: At any time after an acquittal, an arrested, cited or charged person may apply to the court in the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged for an order setting aside the record of the arrest, citation or charge. There is no waiting period and, under ORS 137.225(9), no time limit for making an application. Under ORS 137.225(3)(b) the court shall grant a motion under this paragraph. Oregon calls it a set-aside and there are no separate sealing and expungement tracks: the court sets aside and seals, and under ORS 137.225(4) the conviction, arrest, citation, charge or other proceeding is deemed not to have occurred and the person may answer accordingly any questions relating to its occurrence. The order reaches Oregon court and law enforcement records including the Oregon State Police LEDS system. It does not reach federal or other states' records. Under 2024 Oregon State Police policy a set-aside does not restore firearm rights; a separate restoration process is required. Two statutory carve-outs survive: under ORS 137.225(10) the deemed-not-to-have-occurred rule does not apply in a civil action where truth is an element of a claim or defence, and a party may apply for disclosure; and under ORS 137.225(11) a court may order records reopened on a prosecutor's or defendant's motion supported by affidavit showing good cause, and a prosecuting attorney may unseal a set-aside arrest, citation or charge to initiate a proceeding within the statute of limitations, on written notice to the person.

exclusions: An arrest or citation for driving while under the influence of intoxicants where the charge is dismissed as a result of the person's successful completion of a diversion agreement described in ORS 813.200. ORS 137.225(8)(a).
The dismissal of a citation for a traffic violation. ORS 137.225(8)(b).

A person who, at the time the motion is pending before the court, is under charge of commission of any crime or of contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(C).
Federal and other states' records.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Set Aside a Conviction (ORS 137.225(1)(a) and (1)(b))

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of an offence who has fully complied with and performed the sentence of the court, and whose conviction is described in ORS 137.225(5), may move the court where the conviction was entered for an order setting it aside once eligible under ORS 137.225(1)(b). A person still under supervision as part of that sentence has not fully complied. The tiers run seven years for a Class B felony, five years for a Class C felony, three years for a Class A misdemeanor and one year for a Class B or C misdemeanor or a violation, each measured from the date of conviction or the release from imprisonment for the conviction sought to be set aside, whichever is later. Where the court has reduced the offence classification the applicable period is the one associated with the reduced classification. Where probation was revoked, no application may be made for three years from the revocation or until the person becomes eligible under the ordinary tier, whichever is later. There is no filing fee. Oregon calls it a set-aside and there are no separate sealing and expungement tracks: the court sets aside and seals, and under ORS 137.225(4) the conviction, arrest, citation, charge or other proceeding is deemed not to have occurred and the person may answer accordingly any questions relating to its occurrence. The order reaches Oregon court and law enforcement records including the Oregon State Police LEDS system. It does not reach federal or other states' records. Under 2024 Oregon State Police policy a set-aside does not restore firearm rights; a separate restoration process is required. exclusions: A conviction for a state or municipal traffic offence. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(A).
A Class B felony that is a violation of ORS 166.429, or any crime classified as a person felony under the rules of the Oregon Criminal Justice Commission. ORS 137.225(5)(a).

Criminal mistreatment in the second degree under ORS 163.200 where the victim was 65 or older; criminal mistreatment in the first degree under ORS 163.205 where the victim was 65 or older or the offence constitutes child abuse; endangering the welfare of a minor under ORS 163.575(1)(a) where the offence constitutes child abuse; criminally negligent homicide under ORS 163.145 punishable as a Class C felony; and assault in the third degree under ORS 163.165(1)(h). A conviction of any other offence within the applicable look-back period, excluding motor vehicle violations, a single non-motor-vehicle violation and unlawful possession of a controlled substance constituting a drug enforcement misdemeanour. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) and (7)(b).
A person under charge of any crime, or of contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime, at the time the motion is pending. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(C).

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review approved this track with limitations and made three demands: read the current statute before shipping any tier, add the 2025 monetary-obligations provision to the sentence-completion screen, and never promise firearm restoration. The first is done at primary authority. tracks.legalName: Motion to Set Aside a Contempt of Court Finding (ORS 137.225(1)(a), (1)(b)(B) and (1)(b)(D))
tracks.publicName: Set aside an Oregon contempt of court finding

controllingAuthority.summary: A person found in contempt of court who has fully complied with and performed the sentence for the contempt finding may move to set the finding aside. The enacted text splits contempt across two tiers. A finding of a person in contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime sits in the five-year tier alongside Class C felonies. A finding of contempt not so described sits in the one-year tier alongside Class B and C misdemeanors and violations. Each runs from the date of the finding or the release from imprisonment for the finding sought to be set aside, whichever is later. ORS 137.225(13)(b) defines "order related to abuse or a person crime" as a court order issued under ORS 107.095(1)(c) or (d), 107.700 to 107.735, 124.005 to 124.040, 133.035, 135.247 or 163.760 to 163.777, or a court order arising from a criminal case involving a sex crime, stalking under ORS 163.732, or a person felony or person Class A misdemeanor committed against the person's family or household member as defined in ORS 135.230. Oregon calls it a set-aside and there are no separate sealing and expungement tracks: the court sets aside and seals, and under ORS 137.225(4) the conviction, arrest, citation, charge or other proceeding is deemed not to have occurred and the person may answer accordingly any questions relating to its occurrence. The order reaches Oregon court and law enforcement records including the Oregon State Police LEDS system. It does not reach federal or other states' records. Under 2024 Oregon State Police policy a set-aside does not restore firearm rights; a separate restoration process is required. Two statutory carve-outs survive: under ORS 137.225(10) the deemed-not-to-have-occurred rule does not apply in a civil action where truth is an element of a claim or defence, and a party may apply for disclosure; and under ORS 137.225(11) a court may order records reopened on a prosecutor's or defendant's motion supported by affidavit showing good cause, and a prosecuting attorney may unseal a set-aside arrest, citation or charge to initiate a proceeding within the statute of limitations, on written notice to the person.

exclusions: A person under charge of any crime, or of contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime, at the time the motion is pending. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(C).

A person convicted of any other offence, or found in contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime, within the applicable look-back period, subject to the motor vehicle, single-violation and drug enforcement misdemeanour carve-outs. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) and (7)(b).
Federal and other states' records.

components.notes: Motion and declaration to set aside a contempt finding, from the Oregon Judicial Department Criminal Set-Aside (Adult Cases) packet retained in Edition 1.2 at REV-2026-01. The packet covers contempt findings expressly, listing among those who may use the process a person who was "found in contempt of court".

The proposed order, which ORS 137.225(12) requires the State Court Administrator to publish statewide alongside the motion. On entry the order contains the original arrest or citation charge, the conviction charge if different, the date of charge, the submitting agency and the disposition, and directs sealing. The judge signs it; LegalEase never completes the signature or the court's findings.

ORS 137.225(2)(c): the person forwards a full set of fingerprints to the Department of State Police on a fingerprint card or in any other manner the department specifies. This is mandatory and is the main source of delay. ORS 137.225(2)(d) sets the fee at not more than the actual cost of the record check, and provides that where the department performs only one record check it may charge only one fee regardless of how many counties the person files in.

ORS 137.225(2)(a): a copy of the motion is served on the office of the prosecuting attorney who prosecuted the matter, or who had authority to prosecute if no accusatory instrument was filed. Under ORS 137.225(2)(e) the prosecuting attorney may not charge the person a fee for performing these requirements.

The Oregon State Police set-aside criminal history request and instructions, retained in Edition 1.2, together with the OJD request for a set-aside criminal record check retained at OR-OJD-CLA-SET-ASIDE-CHECK. The LEDS criminal history fixes the offence class, the disposition and the sentence-completion dates, and is obtained before anything is drafted.

The objection diary and what follows. ORS 137.225(2)(a) gives the prosecuting attorney 120 days from the date the motion was filed to object and to notify the court and the person. Under ORS 137.225(3)(b) the court shall grant a motion under subsection (1)(c) or (1)(d), and shall grant a motion under (1)(a) if no objection is received. If an objection is received the court holds a hearing at which the victim may make a statement, and under ORS 137.225(3)(a) the court shall still grant the motion unless it makes written findings by clear and convincing evidence that the person's circumstances and behaviour create a risk to public safety.
Obtain a certified copy of the order, confirm the Oregon State Police sealed its records, and set expectations that county processing can run many months and in some places close to two years.

tracks.legalName: ORS 137.225(1)(d) — the Acquittal and Dismissal Set-Aside Provision
tracks.publicName: The Oregon subsection that covers acquittals and dismissals

controllingAuthority.summary: The controlling review recorded that current ORS 137.225(8) opens "The provisions of subsection (1)(c) or (d) of this section do not apply to", which establishes that a subsection (1)(d) exists and that it is grouped with the arrest, citation and dismissed-charge provisions rather than with convictions, and that its content was not determined and is absent from the internal reference. The content is now determined. Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 349, read at the Oregon Legislature's own channel on 2026-08-06, provides at ORS 137.225(1)(d): "At any time after an acquittal or a dismissal other than a dismissal described in paragraph (c) of this subsection, an arrested, cited or charged person may apply to the court in the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged, for entry of an order setting aside the record of the arrest, citation or charge." Subsection (1)(d) is therefore the acquittal-and-dismissal route, and its substance is carried by the dismissed-charge and acquittal tracks in this memo rather than by a separate packet.

exclusions: The subsection (8) exclusions, which apply to subsection (1)(c) or (d): a DUII arrest or citation dismissed on successful completion of an ORS 813.200 diversion agreement, and the dismissal of a citation for a traffic violation.

Everything else about this slot: it is a statutory provision rather than a distinct participant route, and generating a separate packet for it would duplicate the dismissed-charge and acquittal tracks.
